questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to stay within the European Union.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy. The host institution had sent us all information needed.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I don't think we received any.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I would recommend that you start looking for accommodation as soon as you are notified that you are going to Rome on exchange. It wasn't difficult to find housing but some of the other students ended up paying a lot for a small room.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Search for housing close to the university. Public transportation does not work wonders in Rome.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I don't really remember it that well since I registered almost a year ago. However, I remember thinking it was a bit inconvenient.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could easily send them an email and they were quick to respond.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It is possible to switch courses until a few weeks after the beginning of the semester. That way it is possible to try out different courses.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The EU Law before Courts-course was by far the most challenging and the course most similar to the courses at UCPH as regards the academic level. The other ones weren't difficult.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
Attendance is mandatory. Some teachers just talked for an hour and a half, but there were also courses in which the teaching consisted of discussions. They use teaching assistants so some of the courses had a lot of different professors and teachers.
I had a few multiple choice-exams and that was very different from the exams at UCPH. Not necessarily easier.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
International Organization and Human Rights.
EU Law before Courts: Rights and Procedures.
European Private Law.
International Arbitration: Law and Practice.
Data Protection Law.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would definitely recommend the International Arbitration course since that was my absolute favorite. 

If you enjoy EU Law, you should enroll in the EU Law before Courts course which was an in-depth analysis of the basic EU principles.

The International Organization course was nice since it was mostly Italian students. In the other courses I had there were a lot of exchange students. Furthermore, the classes were at another, bigger campus.

I did not enjoy the European Private Law course. It was unstructured and there was too much preparation for a 6 credit course.

The professor in Data Protection Law was very skilled but the course itself was kind of boring.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Grocery shopping is very cheap and the same goes for going out for dinner.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did not really take part in that. I believe ESN hosted a lot of different social gatherings.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I did not take part in a lot of those social activities except for a few dinners and parties during the first week organized by ESN. The exchange students from UCPH were somehow a bit older than a lot of the other students, Italian as well as other exchange students.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: If you're going there by yourself and don't know anyone there, you should definitely join the ESN since it's a great opportunity to meet people.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go explore Italy with train. Flights to Morocco are also very cheap. The beach is only a 45-minutes train ride away.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Enroll in courses that are taught in English but not created especially for exchange students. Go out in the weekends.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not particularly a cultural difference but the Italians I met were not very good (or comfortable with) speaking English.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: They're all very laid back, don't rush things.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Search for housing as soon as possible!

Be prepared for the public transportation that simply does not work as well as the public transportation in Denmark. We walked a lot.

Learn some of the basic Italian phrases.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not that I can think of.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The experience of living somewhere else.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being away from family and friends.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
